review.question: 2025-07-19 至 2026-07-19 的 loco-manipulation 研究在哪些控制、学习、数据、感知、评测和部署方向取得了可验证进展，其适用边界与未解问题是什么？

relevance.reason: Direct tactile-aware quadrupedal loco-manipulation study with contact-rich real-world tasks.

sections_read.purpose: Identify missing contact observability in vision/proprioception-only systems.
Read the visuotactile diffusion policy and tactile-target low-level controller.

sections_read.locator: IV Experiments and Results > IV-B Experimental Results and Analyze
sections_read.purpose: Verify the 20-rollout task and component comparisons.

research_question: Does predicting and tracking tactile interaction targets improve contact-rich quadrupedal loco-manipulation beyond visual and position-only policies?
contributions: A hierarchical high-level visuotactile diffusion policy and low-level tactile-command-tracking whole-body controller.

method.summary: Human UMI demonstrations train a high-level policy to predict pose, gripper and tactile targets; simulation RL trains a whole-body controller to track pose and tactile commands before zero-shot real deployment.
assumptions: Tactile descriptors transfer from the demonstration gripper to the robot gripper.
Task scenes can be simulated with useful contact cues.

study_context.sample_or_scale: Twenty real rollouts per task and baseline variant.

evaluation.design: Four policy variants separate tactile observation, tactile prediction and low-level tactile tracking.
baselines: visuotactile high level with position-only low level
tactile prediction without tactile low-level tracking

findings.finding: Tactile information adds value at both intent prediction and low-level contact realization, especially where vision cannot reveal contact state.
findings.scope: Three real contact-rich task families on one tactile hardware stack.
findings.locator: IV Experiments and Results > IV-B Experimental Results and Analyze

author_stated.limitation: The tactile representation is not fully integrated and the low-level controller remains limited for fine-grained contact under environmental uncertainty.

reader_inferred.boundary: The results are hardware- and descriptor-specific and do not establish cross-sensor tactile transfer.
reader_inferred.basis: All tasks use one tactile gripper representation and one robot platform.

transfer_boundary: Strongest for contact-rich tasks whose contact evolution is observable through the trained tactile descriptors; cross-hardware generalization is untested.

design_strengths: Component-wise ablations separate high- and low-level tactile roles.
design_risks: Task count and hardware diversity are limited.
critical_appraisal.baseline_fairness: Variants share the same framework and differ by tactile components, enabling attribution.
critical_appraisal.metric_validity: Task success is meaningful; damage-free claims for fruit are qualitative, while chip handling is quantified.
critical_appraisal.reproducibility: Architecture and task definitions are detailed, but sensor calibration and raw data release determine practical replication.
critical_appraisal.external_validity: Limited to one tactile modality and a small set of contact-rich tasks.

evidence_cards.claim: Adding tactile-command tracking at the low level raised insertion success from 0.70 to 0.85, full reorientation-plus-insertion from 0.60 to 0.80, and valve tightening from 0.80 to 0.85.
evidence_cards.relation: Supports tactile targets as executable control signals rather than only high-level observations.
evidence_cards.summary: The paper compares variants with the same tactile-aware high level but different low-level tactile tracking.
evidence_cards.source_context: Finally, comparing Baseline 3 (P3) with our full method demonstrates the benefit of incorporating tactile commands into the low-level policy: our method further increases the success rate from 0.70 to 0.85 on Task 1 insertion (+0.15), from 0.60 to 0.80 on Task 1 whole (+0.20), and from 0.80 to 0.85 on Task 2 (+0.05), and achieves 1.00 on Task 3 (compared to 0.20 for P1).

quantitative.comparator: P3 versus full tactile low-level policy
quantitative.task_or_sample: 20 rollouts on insertion, full sequence and valve tightening
quantitative.locator: IV Experiments and Results > IV-B Experimental Results and Analyze, Table VI

verification.rationale: The cited result sentence gives the same three task comparisons and success-rate changes; the claim stays within those variants and tasks.
